18 A sample of metal is subjected to a force which increases to a maximum value and then
decreases back to zero. A force–extension graph for the sample is shown.
force
Y
X
extension
0
0
When the sample contracts, it follows the same force–extension curve as when it was being
stretched.
What is the behaviour of the metal between X and Y?
A
both elastic and plastic
B
not elastic and not plastic
C
elastic but not plastic
D
plastic but not elastic

hints: Look at the shape of the force-extension graph: straight from 0 to X, then curved from X to Y, with point Y at maximum force.
Recall that elastic behaviour means the extension returns to zero when the force is removed, while plastic behaviour leaves a permanent extension.
Check what happens on unloading between Y and 0: it follows the same curve backwards with no loop, so decide if any permanent extension remains even though Hooke's law is no longer obeyed.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: loading goes from 0 to Y, with X marking the end of the straight-line section, and unloading from Y follows exactly the same force-extension curve back to the origin.
State the test for elastic behaviour: a material is elastic if it returns to its original length, so $extension = 0$ when $force = 0$ after removal of load.

State the test for plastic behaviour: a material is plastic if some extension remains when the force is zero, which would appear as the unloading curve meeting the extension axis away from the origin.
Apply to the region between X and Y: the graph curves, so $F$ is no longer proportional to $x$ and Hooke's law is exceeded, but because unloading retraces the curve there is no residual extension.
Conclude that the deformation is recoverable and therefore elastic, with no permanent plastic set. This is option C.

A.explanation: It cannot be both because the unloading retraces the loading curve to zero extension, so no permanent plastic extension is left.

B.explanation: It must be elastic because the sample returns to zero extension when force returns to zero.

C.explanation: The sample returns along the same curve to the origin so it is elastic with no permanent set, but the curve between X and Y is non-linear so Hooke's law is not obeyed.

D.explanation: It cannot be plastic because plastic deformation would leave a non-zero extension at zero force and a hysteresis loop, which is not observed.
